articleTitle: The representation dimension of Schur algebras: the tame case
abstract: We show that all Schur algebras (classical, infinitesimal and quantum) of tame representation type have representation dimension 3.

articleTitle: Corrigendum The degree of the divisor of jumping rational curves (Quart. J. Math. 52 (2001), 367–383)
An infinite loop space structure on the nerve of spin bordism categories
abstract: In this paper, we exhibit an infinite loop space structure on the nerve of certain spin bordism 2‐categories and compare it with the classifying space of suitably stabilized spin mapping class groups. We show that the stable spin mapping class group has the homology of an infinite loop space. In order to do this, we adapt Harer's homology stabilization results for spin mapping class groups to a setting compatible with the methods Tillmann used to prove that the classifying space of (non‐spin) mapping class groups has the homology of an infinite loop space. We also study a variant of the spin mapping class groups, due to Masbaum, and show that its homology also stabilizes as the genus tends to infinity.

articleTitle: On the approximation numbers of Sobolev embeddings on singular domains and trees
abstract: Upper and lower bounds are determined for a function which counts the approximation numbers of the Sobolev embedding W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,p</sup> (Ω)/C ↪L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup> (Ω)/C, for a wide class of domains Ω of finite volume in R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> and 1 < p < ∞. Results on the distribution of the eigenvalues of the Neumann Laplacian in L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(Ω) are special consequences.

articleTitle: Erratum
Inertia Orbifolds, Configuration Spaces and the Ghost Loop Space
abstract: In this paper we define and study the ghost loop orbifold L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>X of an orbifold X consisting of those loops that remain constant in the coarse moduli space of X. We construct a configuration space model for L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>X using an idea of G. Segal. From this we exhibit the relation between the Hochschild and cyclic homologies of the inertia orbifold of X (that generate the so‐called twisted sectors in string theory) and the ordinary and equivariant homologies of L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>X. We also show how this clarifies the relation between Chen–Ruan orbifold cohomology, Hochschild homology, and periodic cyclic homology.

articleTitle: Non‐principal blocks with one simple module
abstract: We give a general construction which shows that a large class of quantum complete intersections can be realized as the basic algebras of non‐principal blocks of finite groups. We investigate the Ext rings of these algebras. We describe how to construct a finite p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">′</sup>‐covering for one of these quantum complete intersections, which supports a Hopf algebra structure which is neither commutative nor cocommutative in general. We use this to investigate a problem concerning the definition of nucleus for a non‐principal block.

articleTitle: An additive measure in o-minimal expansions of fields
abstract: Given an o-minimal structure M which expands a field, we define, for each positive integer d, a real-valued additive measure on a Boolean algebra of subsets of M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup> and we prove that all the definable sets included in the finite part Fin(M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup>) of M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup> are measurable. When the domain of M is R we obtain Lebesgue measure, but restricted to a proper subalgebra of that of the Lebesgue measurable sets (the Jordan measurable sets). Our measure has good logical properties, being invariant under elementary extensions and under expansions of the language. In the final part of the paper we consider the problem of defining an analogue of the Haar measure for definably compact groups.

articleTitle: When absolute continuity on C‐algebras is automatically uniform
abstract: Let A be a C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐algebra and let K be a relatively weakly compact subset of the dual of A. Let ψbe a positive linear functional on A such that, for each φin K, φis strongly absolutely continuous with respect to ψ. Then, for each ε> 0, there exists δ> 0, such that for each x in the closed unit ball of A, ψ(xx<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> +x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>x)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> ≤δimplies |φ(x) |≤εfor every φ∈K. This result is extended to the situation where K is a σ‐bounded set of weakly compact operators from A to a Banach space Y.

articleTitle: Multilinear extensions of Grothendieck's theorem
abstract: We introduce a new class of multilinear p-summing operators, which we call multiple p-summing. Using them, we can prove several multilinear generalizations of Grothendieck's ‘fundamental theorem of the metric theory of tensor products’. As an application we prove a vector-valued Littlewood's inequality.

articleTitle: Irreducible subgroups of algebraic groups
abstract: A closed subgroup of a semisimple algebraic group G is said to be G‐irreducible if it lies in no proper parabolic subgroup of G. We prove a number of results concerning such subgroups. Firstly they have only finitely many overgroups in G; secondly, with some specified exceptions, there exist G‐irreducible subgroups of type A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>; and thirdly, we prove an embedding theorem for G‐irreducible subgroups.

articleTitle: The number of knots and links with the same 2‐fold branched covering
abstract: We give a nearly complete solution of the problem of how many different knots and links in the 3‐sphere, and more generally in homology 3‐spheres, can have the same hyperbolic 3‐manifold as their common 2‐fold branched covering. This number depends on the number of components of the links. We show that the best possible upper bound is nine for knots and for 2‐component links, and three for links with more than two components.

articleTitle: On the number of links and link polynomials
abstract: We use a recent method of Sundberg and Thistlethwaite to improve Welsh's upper bound on the rate of growth of the number of links of given crossing number and to show that the number of polynomials of alternating links drops off exponentially in the crossing number compared to the number of such links.

articleTitle: Orbits of normal basis generators
abstract: Let L/K be a finite‐dimensional Galois field extension with Galois group G, B the set of normal basis generators for this extension, and C={γ ∈L∣γ B=B}. Then C is a group under multiplication. This group was introduced and characterized in Theorem 1.15 of a well‐known paper ‘Primitive normal bases for finite fields’ by H. W. Lenstra Jr. and R. J. Schoof. This result was stated in that paper without a proof. The purpose of this paper is to give a proof of the theorem.

articleTitle: The RICCI curvature of submanifolds and its applications
abstract: We prove the non‐existence of stable currents or compact stable minimal submanifolds for a class of submanifolds in a Euclidean space which satisfies an operative condition involving the Ricci curvature. In addition, we prove that these submanifolds are homeomorphic to the sphere. Moreover, we give examples which show that our result is optimal.

articleTitle: A new mean‐value result for Dirichlet L‐functions and polynomials

articleTitle: Uniform dimension of modules
abstract: Let M be a module which has finite uniform dimension and let K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>(1 ≤ i ≤ n) be a finite collection of submodules of M such that 0 = K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> ∩···∩ K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>. Then the uniform dimension u(M) of M is the sum of the uniform dimensions of the factor modules M/K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>(1 ≤ i ≤ n) if and only if K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> is a complement of K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> ∩···∩ K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i−1</inf> ∩ K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i+1</inf> ∩···∩ K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> in M for each 1 ≤ i ≤ n. In case K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> is P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>-prime for some prime ideal P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> for each 1 ≤ i ≤ n, the prime ideals P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> (1 ≤ i ≤ n) are distinct and 0 ≠ K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> ∩···∩ K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i−1</inf> ∩ K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i+1</inf> ∩···∩ K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> for each 1 ≤ i ≤ n, then it is shown that u(M) = ∑<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i=1</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> u(L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>/(L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> ∩ K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>)) for certain submodules L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> (1 ≤ i ≤ n) of M.

articleTitle: Homology of spaces of smooth embeddings
abstract: It is shown how the methods of the calculus of embeddings can be used to calculate, or help with the calculation of, the homology of spaces of smooth embeddings.

articleTitle: A New Identity for (q;q)∞10 with an Application to Ramanujan's Partition Congruence Modulo 11
abstract: A new identity for the tenth power of the Dedekind eta‐funtion η(z) is established. This is used to give a short proof of Ramanujan's congruence p(11n+6) ≡0 (mod 11) and to prove the lacunarity of η<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup>(z). Various related identities, many connected to Eisenstein series and some from Ramanujan's lost notebook, are established.

articleTitle: The power structure of finite p-groups satisfying conditions like those of Lazard
abstract: Lazard proved that finitely generated pro-p groups satisfying γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>(G) ≤ G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ph</sup> are p-adic analytic if m < p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sup>. Recent work has given a very thorough understanding of the finite p-groups that satisfy this condition with h = 1. In this paper, we consider pro-p groups that show that those results cannot be extended to the case of h = 2 for m ≥ 2p − 1. We do extend many of the results to this case when m ≤ 2p − 3 as well as under some weaker hypotheses.

articleTitle: A useful estimate for the decreasing rearrangement of the sum of functions
abstract: Given f=∑<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n∈N</inf> f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, where {f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>}<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> are measurable functions, we show that f<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>(3t)≤∑<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> ( f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>(t) +1/t ∫<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cnt</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sup>f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>(s) ds ), where {c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>}<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n∈N</inf> are positive numbers such that ∑<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>=1. Several consequences in the setting of weighted Lorentz spaces are also given.

articleTitle: Explicit upper bounds for |L(1,χ)|for primitive characters χ
abstract: We give explicit upper bounds for |L(1,χ)|for primitive Dirichlet characters χ. These bounds depend on the behaviour of χat primes p in a given set S of primes.

articleTitle: On Weakly‐Compactly Generated Asplund Banach spaces
abstract: In this paper we give a sufficient and necessary condition for a Banach space to be weakly‐compactly generated and Asplund. This condition links the weak<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> and the norm topologies of its dual.

articleTitle: On the Baum–Connes conjecture in the real case
abstract: Let Γ be a countable discrete group. We prove that if the usual Baum–Connes conjecture is valid for Γ, then the real form of Baum–Connes is also valid for Γ. This is relevant to proving that Baum–Connes implies the stable Gromov–Lawson–Rosenberg conjecture about Riemannian metrics of positive scalar curvature.

articleTitle: On a new construction of special Lagrangian immersions in complex Euclidean space
abstract: We construct new special Lagrangian submanifolds in complex Euclidean space using a pair of minimal Legendrian submanifolds in odd‐dimensional spheres and certain Lagrangian surface belonging to a family that can be considered as a generalization of the special Lagrangian surfaces in complex Euclidean plane. Our examples include those invariant under the standard action of SO(p+1)×SO(q+1) on C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> = C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p+1</sup> ×C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q+1</sup>, n=p+q+2.

articleTitle: Separating ideals in group algebras
abstract: Let G be a non‐compact locally compact group and let A be a unital Banach algebra. We show that the only separating ideal in L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>(G,A) is {0}. This entails that every epimorphism onto L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>(G,A) and every derivation on L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>(G,A) is continuous.

articleTitle: Paschke duality for real and graded C‐algebras
abstract: Shortly after Brown, Douglas and Fillmore introduced their interpretation of K‐homology, it was pointed out by Paschke that the BDF groups are in fact the K‐theory groups of a certain essential commutant algebra. This note describes a version of this construction which is appropriate for real and/or graded C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐algebras.

articleTitle: On Roth's theorem concerning a cube and three cubes of primes
abstract: In this paper, we prove that with at most O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1271/1296+ε</sup>) exceptions, all positive integers up to N are the sum of a cube and three cubes of primes. This improves an earlier result O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">169/170</sup>) of the first author and the classical result O(NL<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">‐A</sup>) of Roth.

articleTitle: Derivations from Banach function algebras
abstract: We study the structure of derivations D : Alg<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf> C [X] → A, where A is a function algebra defined on a compact subset of C such that A contains C [X]. We show that, under certain conditions on the algebra A, all such derivations are zero. We give examples to show the necessity of these conditions.

articleTitle: The conjugate dimension of algebraic numbers
abstract: We find sharp upper and lower bounds for the degree of an algebraic number in terms of the Q‐dimension of the space spanned by its conjugates. For all but seven non‐negative integers n the largest degree of an algebraic number whose conjugates span a vector space of dimension n is equal to 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>n!. The proof, which covers also the seven exceptional cases, uses a result of Feit on the maximal order of finite subgroups of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(Q); this result depends on the classification of finite simple groups. In particular, we construct an algebraic number of degree 1152 whose conjugates span a vector space of dimension only 4. We extend our results in two directions. We consider the problem when Q is replaced by an arbitrary field, and prove some general results. In particular, we again obtain sharp bounds when the ground field is a finite field, or a cyclotomic extension Q(ω <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ℓ</inf>) of Q. Also, we look at a multiplicative version of the problem by considering the analogous rank problem for the multiplicative group generated by the conjugates of an algebraic number.

articleTitle: Polynomial loops on spheres
abstract: The space of algebraic (Laurent polynomial) free loops on a sphere is filtered by the degree. It is shown that this filtration admits a natural stable splitting that corresponds to the known splitting, as a wedge of Thom spaces, of the homotopy-equivalent space of continuous loops.

articleTitle: On the Depth of Cohomology Modules
abstract: We study the cohomology modules H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sup>(G,R) of a p‐group G acting on a ring R of characteristic p, for i>0. In particular, we are interested in the Cohen–Macaulay property and the depth of H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sup>(G,R) regarded as an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</sup>‐module. We first determine the support of H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sup>(G,R), which turns out to be independent of i. Then we study the Cohen–Macaulay property for H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>(G,R). Further results are restricted to the special case that G is cyclic and R is the symmetric algebra of a vector space on which G acts. We determine the depth of H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sup>(G,R) for i odd and obtain results in certain cases for i even. Along the way, we determine the degrees in which the transfer map Tr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</sup> R →R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</sup> has non‐zero image.

articleTitle: A Geometric Characterization of Automatic Monoids
abstract: It is well known that automatic groups can be characterized using geometric properties of their Cayley graphs. Along the same line of thought, we provide a geometric characterization of automatic monoids. This involves working with a slightly strengthened definition of an automatic monoid which is still a proper generalization of the concept of an automatic group. The two definitions coincide in the case of right cancellative monoids for which a particularly simple characterization is obtained.

articleTitle: Acyclic groups and wild arcs
abstract: We discuss two classes of acyclic groups that are commutator subgroups of finitely presented groups with infinite cyclic abelianization. The first is algebraic and includes groups first exhibited by Baumslag and Gruenberg, of which it is shown that Epstein's acyclic group is a special case. The second class is geometric, and is shown to include a number of wild arc groups in the literature.

articleTitle: Complex structures on affine motion groups
abstract: We study existence of complex structures on semidirect products g ⊕<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ρ</inf> v, where g is a real Lie algebra and ρ is a representation of g on v. Our first examples, the Euclidean algebra e(3) and the Poincaré algebra e(2, 1), carry complex structures obtained by deformation of a regular complex structure on sl (2, C). We also exhibit a complex structure on the Galilean algebra G(3, 1). We construct next a complex structure on g ⊕<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ρ</inf> v starting with one on g under certain compatibility assumptions on ρ.As an application of our results we obtain that there exists k ∈ {0, 1} such that (S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup> × E(n) admits a left invariant complex structure, where S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> is the circle and E(n) denotes the Euclidean group. We also prove that the Poincaré group P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4k+3</sup> has a natural left invariant complex structure.In case dim g = dim v, there is an adapted complex structure on g ⊕<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ρ</inf> v precisely when ρ determines a flat, torsion-free connection on g. If ρ is self-dual, g ⊕<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ρ</inf> v carries a natural symplectic structure as well. If, moreover, ρ comes from a metric connection then g ⊕<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ρ</inf> v possesses a pseudo-Kähler structure.We prove that the tangent bundle TG of a Lie group G carrying a flat torsion-free connection ∇ and a parallel complex structure possesses a hypercomplex structure. More generally, by an iterative procedure, we can obtain Lie groups carrying a family of left invariant complex structures which generate any prescribed real Clifford algebra.

articleTitle: Characterizations of the finite quadric Veroneseans Vn2n
abstract: We generalize and complete several characterizations of the finite quadric Veroneseans surveyed in Hirschfeld and Thas, General Galois Geometries, OUP, 1991. Our main result is a characterization of the quadric Veronesean V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n</sup> in terms of the subspaces of the ambient projective space generated by the sub‐Veroneseans isomorphic to V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n−1</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n−1</sup>. We also obtain, as an application, a completely new characterization of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n</sup>.

articleTitle: An Isomorphism of Quantum Semimartingale Algebras
abstract: We give details of a *‐linear bijection between adapted (in the sense of Hudson and Parthasarathy) and vacuum‐adapted quantum stochastic integrals. This provides new insight into Attal's remarkable transformation of quantum semimartingales, by showing that it factorizes in a natural manner. The Banach *‐algebras of regular quantum and Ω‐semimartingales are consequently isomorphic, and an intrinsic characterisation of Ω‐semimartingales is obtained as an application of this fact. Various formulae occurring in quantum stochastic calculus are shown to have a more natural appearance in the vacuum‐adapted framework. We finish by providing the full generalization of this theory to higher dimensions.

articleTitle: Integer points on the dilation of a subanalytic surface
abstract: Let Ω ⊂R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> be a compact subanalytic set of dimension 2 and t≥1. This paper gives an upper bound as t→∞ for the number of integer points on the homothetic dilation tΩ of Ω that do not reside on any connected semialgebraic subset of tΩ of positive dimension. Implications for the density of rational points on Ω are also elaborated.
